Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. The players are out in the middle. Martin Guptill and Finn Allen to open for the Kiwis. Kyle Mayers to bowl first.
... The Run Chase ...

Right then! The pitch got better in the end to bat and the slower balls are working well to make an impact for the bowlers. Still, this is a very tight contest and the team who plays the best will win the series. The T20I went the visitors' way, will it be the same for them? We will find out soon. Stay tuned for the chase.

Kyle Mayers is here for a quick word. He says that he feels lucky and he thinks he batted well. Adds that after losing early wickets in the last game they were more careful in this one and they started slowly in the first powerplay as the plan was to tackle Boult and Southee and they did good in the end. Says that he feels very happy after his century and he's glad the crowd enjoyed it. Finishes by saying that they need to do well with the ball and defend the score.

A bit frustrating outing from the Kiwi bowlers! They didn't break the stand early on and allowed the opposition to get away. Once they got their wickets, they then got the hammering from Nicholas Pooran. They took wickets at the other end but Pooran alone made a huge lot of difference to the score. The slower balls helped them mainly to keep under control but now have to chase a huge score.

What an innings it was from Pooran! An innings that helped West Indies end on a high. The start though was very slow from the hosts. They started slowly but Mayers took the charge soon later. Hope played second fiddle to him. The duo notched a 173 opening stand with Hope scoring a fifty and Mayers scoring a wonderful ton. They fell in quick succession but it was then Pooran's inning that helped them get past 290. Pooran was at his best after quite a few innings and this could potentially be a game-changing knock. Not to forget that little cameo from Alzarri Joseph that helped them get past 300.
An excellent batting performance from West Indies! A performance that was dearly needed by them and most importantly bat the full quota.

Bowls it outside off again, Shai Hope lets this one go as well.
An outswinger outside off, slightly shorter, left alone.
Touch fuller this time, on off, Kyle Mayers flicks it to mid-wicket for one.
Delivers it on a length again, Shai Hope flicks it but finds the fielder at square leg.
On a length and down the middle, Shai Hope blocks it away.
On a length and on middle, Kyle Mayers flicks it but gets his thigh and towards backward square leg for a leg bye.
Serves it on a length and down the middle, Kyle Mayers defends it again towards short mid-wicket.
Goes fuller this time, quicker too, Kyle Mayers blocks it towards short covers.
Slightly shorter, around off, defended to short covers.
Tim Southee starts with a maiden. On a length and on off, Shai Hope defends it solidly.
This one lands outside off and nips back in, Shai Hope looks to defend it but misses. Good delivery.
On a length and on off, Shai Hope eases it to point. Four dots in a row now.
This is on a length and outside off swinging it away, Shai Hope leaves it alone.
A dot as this is defended towards point again.
Southee starts with a length ball outside off, Shai Hope defends it to point.
Tim Southee to bowl from the other end.
On a length and down the middle, Kyle Mayers looks to drive it but gets an inside edge towards the keeper. A dot to finish the over.
This one is outside off as well, Kyle Mayers leaves it alone.
On a length and outside off, left alone by Kyle Mayers.
Fuller and on leg, Shai Hope looks to tuck it but gets his pads and towards the leg side. They cross for a leg bye.
Bowls it on off, Shai Hope drives but finds the fielder at covers.
FOUR! Shai Hope gets off the mark with a boundary! This one lands fuller and on leg, Hope gives it a fine tickle as the ball races away the fine leg fence.

We are all set for the action. The players are out in the middle. Shai Hope and Kyle Mayers are the openers for West Indies. Trent Boult to start with the ball. Before the start, the Windies players will take the knee in support of the 'BLM' movement.

Pitch Report - Samuel Badree thinks there will be a bit of rain. Adds it is a new pitch but looks similar to the other games. Tells there is a grass cover, the bowlers will have more bounce. Shares the new ball bowlers will enjoy but the batters will have runs on offer as well.

Kevin Sinclair is up for a chat. He says that he is happy to get this opportunity. Adds that the skipper gives him a lot of confidence as he lets him know what the team requires from him. Tells that he just tries to be patient and work on his basics. Shares that they just need to focus on their game and do the basics right.

Nicholas Pooran says that they wanted to bowl but they will try and put good pressure with the bat first and do their best. Further says that this is an important game and they will hope to win the series. Finally says that they will play with the same team.

Tom Latham the skipper of New Zealand says that they will bowl first as it's a fresh wicket. Further says that they can put the ball to work well and bat afterward. Says that it was worrying about how the last order of West Indies performed well the other day and Finn Allen was great. Mentions that will hope to put good performance with the ball. Finally says about Kane Williamson's injury and Ferguson is in for Phillips.

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Martin Guptill, Finn Allen, Devon Conway, Tom Latham (C/WK), Daryl Mitchell, James Neesham, Michael Bracewell, Mitchell Santner, Tim Southee, Lockie Ferguson (In for Glenn Phillips), Trent Boult.

West Indies (Unchanged Playing XI) - Shai Hope (WK), Kyle Mayers, Shamarh Brooks, Brandon King, Keacy Carty, Nicholas Pooran (C), Jason Holder, Yannic Cariah, Akeal Hosein, Alzarri Joseph, Kevin Sinclair.
TOSS - New Zealand have won the toss and elected to BOWL first.

New Zealand's top order fumbled a bit as well but Finn Allen was the star with the bat who scored 96 runs as the visitors reached a par total of 212 runs. The pace duo of Trent Boult and Tim Southee ran through the opposition's lineup to claim 7 wickets. They would hope to win this series on Caribbean soil.  Whose side are you on?
